proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity or power of an obligation to bind, direct, or compel action. It is internally grounded in the obligation-bearer relation and is not merely an external label. It is not yet actualized until the agent acts or fails to act; it is thus a realizable entity that is a disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than a role (externally grounded) or a quality (non-realizable). It inheres in the bearer of the obligation. It can be realized in compliance processes or enforcement processes. This distinguishes it from the obligation itself (modeled as LegalObligation, a Role/SDC) and from the quality of being obligated.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016): it is an internally grounded realizable specifically dependent continuant inhering in a bearer, realizable in processes of compliance or enforcement.
As a Disposition, NormativeForce is also a subclass of Specifically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000020), which all Dispositions are.

open_questions: Is 'normative force' being treated as a general class (kind of disposition any obligation can have) or as a specific individual instance tied to a particular obligation? If the latter, an individual inhering in a specific LegalObligation individual would be more appropriate.

Should NormativeForce be modeled as a subclass of the existing LegalObligation (BFO_0000023 Role) class, or kept as an independent disposition that inheres in the bearer of an obligation? These are different ontological claims.
Is normative force always legal, or does this concept also cover moral obligations? If legal only, a more specific parent like 'LegalNormativeForce' under NormativeForce may be warranted.
What process is NormativeForce realized in? Compliance behavior (BehavioralLegalManifestation) seems plausible given existing classes — should we assert that relation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'normative force of an obligation' refers to the binding, action-guiding power that an obligation exerts on its bearer — the capacity to compel conduct. In BFO 2020, Disposition (BFO_0000016) is the best fit: it is a realizable specifically dependent continuant that is internally grounded in its bearer (the agent who holds the obligation), and it is not yet actualized until manifested in behavior. This contrasts with Role (BFO_0000023), which is externally grounded in social context, and Quality (BFO_0000019), which is non-realizable. The normative force inheres in the agent bearing the obligation and is realized in compliance or enforcement processes. The existing class LegalObligation is typed as Role/SDC, which captures the social relational status of being obligated; NormativeForce captures the distinct dispositional capacity that flows from that status. Minting NormativeForce as a new Disposition subclass is the conservative, BFO-consistent choice.
